thread:
josh: Ran a daytime sweep comparing RoPE variants (linear / NTK / YARN) on mixtral-8b with longctx loads. Seeing perplexity drift after ~5k tokens on NTK and YARN for a subset of prompts. kernel selection looks like it switched to the fallback slow path around that point. attaching quick notes.
anya: can you paste the perf snippet you saw? rough numbers ok.
josh: sure — run used: `--model mixtral-8b --rope ntk --seq_len 8192 --batching adaptive`.
josh: profiler tail:
```
[PROF] step 4800 seq=5120 kernel=matmul_fallback time=37.8ms
[PROF] step 4801 seq=5121 kernel=matmul_opt time=18.2ms
[PROF] kv_memory.used=12.6GB kv.evicted=0
[METRIC] perplexity: baseline=12.1 -> 15.8 after step 4800
```
robin: hmm kernel flip at 5120 is suspicious. our kernel selector has a branch: if seq_len > 4096 choose head-shard kernel; fall back on ntk-safe matmul when config mismatch. did you pin kernels?
josh: not explicitly. used `--kernel=auto` which should pick optimized kernels but tuner seems to misclassify mixtral NTK at that seq.
caroline: could be batching heuristics too — adaptive batching might create micro-batches that change compute pattern and trigger different kernel paths. what's the batch size distribution?
josh: distribution roughly: most requests 1-2, occasional bursts up to 8. adaptive merged them into 6/7 batches briefly.
anya: iirc we turned on prefix-KV caching; that plus large batches can push effective key dims > threshold for some fused kernels.
robin: can you repro with batching disabled? `--batching=max_batch=1` to isolate.
josh: ran that quick — with batching off kernel stayed `matmul_opt`, and perplexity stayed stable (12.3 -> 12.5). so batching looks correlated.
caroline: interesting. suggests batching heuristics trigger a kernel route that isn't fully NTK-safe at longctx. we might need an explicit safety gate: if rope_variant in {ntk,yarn} and seq_len>4096 force kernel=matmul_opt_ntk-safe.
perf-bot: auto-run created perf job 2109876550: mixtral-8b ntk yarn sweep (longctx). link: https://ci.redwood/perf/2109876550
josh: here's minimal repro command for infra tests:
```
./run_infer --model mixtral-8b --rope ntk --seq_len 6144 --kernel=auto --batching=adaptive --prefix_cache=on
```
robin: can you capture head/kv dims and kernel selection stacktrace? `RUNTIME_DEBUG=1 RUNTIME_TRACE=kernel_select` should log the decision.
josh: captured — snippet:
```
[TRACE] kernel_select: model=mixtral-8b heads=32 kv_dim=1280 seq=6144 batching=adaptive
[TRACE] candidate_kernels=[matmul_opt,matmul_fallback,fused_head_kernel]
[TRACE] choose=matmul_fallback reason=kv_dim*seq > 7e6
```
anya: `kv_dim*seq > 7e6` heuristic is too coarse for NTK/YARN variants; kv_dim scales differently with head-slicing in mixtral.
caroline: agree. proposal: replace static threshold with model-aware profiling table keyed by (model, rope_variant, head_dim) and prefer the kernel with best measured latency under similar batch patterns. fall back only on OOM-safe kernel otherwise.
robin: +1. also add an override in deployment config so Dedicated customers can lock kernel selection per model if they care about quality/stability.
josh: quick patch idea:
```
if (rope_variant in ntk_like && seq>4096) force_kernel = profile_table.lookup(model,rope_variant,head_dim)
```
caroline: also consider kv-eviction tuning: if prefix cache retains >N entries for longctx it bloats kv_dim effective cost. maybe cap retained prefixes to last 4k tokens for ntk variants.
anya: we should run a controlled sweep: disable adaptive batching, run adaptive batching with kernel safety gate, and run current config. collect perplexity + p50 latency + kernel_switch count.
perf-bot: scheduled matrix jobs: 2109876562 (no-batching), 2109876567 (batching+gate), 2109876572 (baseline). Results will auto-post.
deploy-bot: note: staging rollout paused for mixtral-ntk longctx after yesterday's canary alert.
josh: ok next steps: (1) implement model-aware kernel threshold table PR, (2) add batching->kernel safety gate, (3) short-term mitigate by disabling adaptive batching for mixtral-ntk on Dedicated until gate lands. I'll open PRs and link here.
robin: thanks. self-assigning review on kernel selector PR.
caroline: assign me for rollout plan and config flag docs.
anya: I'll own the perf matrix analysis once jobs complete.
josh: thanks all. will post PR numbers shortly.
